extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working in arithmetic geometry / anabelian geometry and readers of Mochizuki's IUT papers
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing and comparing mono-theta and Gaussian monoids in the IUT (Inter-Universal Teichmüller) framework, including Kummer-theoretic isomorphisms, compatibility with group actions, functoriality, and splittings up to torsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Split Theta Monoids (Kummer-derived isomorphisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: By forming Kummer classes relative to the Frobenioid structure of †F_v and applying the description of the exterior cyclotome of a mono-theta environment, one obtains collections of isomorphisms of monoids Ψ†F Θ_v,α ∼→ Ψι_env(MΘ*) and ∞Ψ†F Θ_v,α ∼→ ∞Ψι_env(MΘ*) which are well-defined up to composition with an inner automorphism and compatible with the respective conjugation actions by ΠX(MΘ*) and the splittings up to torsion on the monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These isomorphisms arise from Kummer/Galois cohomology (N-th roots of unity) and are described by Proposition 1.3 and Example 3.2. They are only determined up to inner automorphism; compatibility with conjugation actions and splittings up to torsion is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant Monoids (Kummer-derived identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming Kummer classes for †F_v and applying Proposition 1.3 yields an isomorphism of monoids Ψ†Cv ∼→ Ψcns(MΘ*) which is well-defined up to composition with an inner automorphism and compatible with the respective conjugation actions by ΠX(MΘ*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to split theta monoids but for the 'constant' (cns) portion; references include [FrdII], IUTchI remarks and Proposition 1.3. Inner-automorphism indeterminacy and conjugation-compatibility are explicit requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradiality of Split Theta Monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: Each isomorphism of projective systems of mono-theta environments (MΘ*(Πv) ∼→ MΘ*(†F_v)) induces compatible collections of isomorphisms between the associated ΠX, Ψenv, ∞Ψenv, and Gv objects; the top horizontal arrows are isomorphisms of topological groups, lower/middle horizontals are isomorphisms of ind-topological monoids, and the latter are compatible with splittings up to torsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functors/algorithms (Propositions 1.2, 3.1 etc.) must be functorial with respect to isomorphisms of projective systems, and the induced collections should be compatible (in evident sense) with arbitrary automorphisms of the underlying pair (ind-topological monoid equipped with a topological group action), up to Ism-multiples. Pay attention to where '×' denotes units and quotients by torsion are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniradiality of Constant Monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: Analogously, isomorphisms of projective systems induce compatible collections of isomorphisms for constant monoids (Ψcns, ∞Ψcns, Gv, ΠX); however, the algorithm (as given) only admits a uniradial formulation and depends on the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism, hence fails to be compatible with certain automorphisms of the underlying pair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit statement of incompatibility: the constant-monoid algorithm relies on cyclotomic rigidity (Corollary 1.11(b)) and therefore cannot be formulated in the fully multiradial (automorphism-compatible) way without additional modifications. Remarks indicate potential remedies developed later (log-shells, IUTchIII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with Splittings up to Torsion
rubrics_metrics.description: The constructions (especially of Ψ-type monoids and Gaussian monoids) must be compatible with splittings up to torsion: many monoids admit splittings up to torsion which the restriction and comparison isomorphisms must respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Proposition 3.1(i), Corollary 2.8, and multiple corollaries in §3. Compatibility with splittings up to torsion is repeatedly emphasized as a necessary coherence condition for isomorphisms and restriction maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetrizing Isomorphisms and Conjugate Synchronization (labels & F_l^±-symmetry)
rubrics_metrics.description: For labeled copies indexed by cusp-labels t ∈ LabCusp±(ΠX(MΘ*)), one must construct F_l^±-symmetrizing isomorphisms (induced by ΔX(MΘ*)-outer action of ΔC(MΘ*)) that identify labeled data across labels while preserving a bijective link with the labels and enabling conjugate synchronization relative to a single basepoint ΠX(MΘ*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The symmetrizing isomorphisms are required to be compatible with label-identifications and to be well-defined up to composition with an inner automorphism independent of the label index. The combinatorial model (ordered vs unordered two-point set) illustrates pitfalls of naive quotienting and the need for descent-type symmetrization rather than coarse collapsing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gaussian Monoids (value-profiles and generated submonoids)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Gaussian monoids Ψξ(MΘ*) (and ∞Ψξ) parametrized by value-profiles ξ (elements of a finite set of cardinality (2l)^l). Each Ψξ(MΘ*) is generated (up to torsion subtleties) by Ψ×_cns(MΘ*) labeled factors times ξ^N (or ξ^Q≥0 for ∞-version); Ψ2l·ξ is independent of the value-profile ξ. Restriction operations give compatible morphisms between these submonoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses restriction algorithms (Corollary 2.8) and symmetrizing isomorphisms; roots are uniquely determined up to N-torsion. Compatibility of actions by Gv(MΘ*) and equalities among Ψ2l·ξ for distinct ξ are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant-monoid Diagonal and Splitting for Gaussian Monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: The diagonal submonoid Ψcns(MΘ*)|Fl| identifies with a graph-of-an-isomorphism (Ψcns(MΘ*)0 ∼→ Ψcns(MΘ*)|Fl|) compatible with labeled Gv-actions; restriction to zero-labeled evaluation points yields splittings up to torsion of each Gaussian monoid Ψξ and ∞Ψξ consistent with Proposition 3.1(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies how one gets canonical (up to torsion) splittings for Gaussian monoids via diagonal/zero-labeled embeddings; must be compatible with other restriction isomorphisms and with previously established splittings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenioid-theoretic Gaussian Monoids (transfer & compatibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: When MΘ* = MΘ*(†F_v) (†F_v tempered Frobenioid), isomorphisms determine submonoids ΨFξ(†F_v) and ∞ΨFξ(†F_v) inside (Ψ†Cv )|t| via the identifications from Corollary 3.5. These Frobenioid-theoretic Gaussian monoids carry Gv(MΘ*)-actions and inherit splittings up to torsion; the constructions are well-defined up to composition with a single inner automorphism of ΠX(MΘ*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition of Kummer isomorphisms with restriction maps is required; keep track of inner-automorphism indeterminacy and equalities involving Ψ2l·ξ. Notation ΨFgau(†F_v) and ∞ΨFgau(†F_v) used for collections over value-profiles ξ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois compatibility / Galois evaluation (Kummer theory link)
rubrics_metrics.description: The monoids ∞Ψ (not just Ψ) must satisfy Galois functoriality: Kummer theory supplies evaluation maps relating Frobenioid-theoretic theta/gaussian monoids to group-theoretic ones, giving a diagram (Fig.3.1) connecting 'Frobenioid-theoretic theta monoids' =⇒ 'group-theoretic theta monoids' ⇓_Galois_evaluation 'Frobenioid-theoretic Gaussian monoids' (and via forgetting, post-anabelian 'abstract monoids').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central organizing principle: Kummer theory relates Frobenius-like monoid structures to étale-like group structures via evaluation at torsion points; constructions must respect this Galois evaluation. The 'forget' arrow yields abstract monoids stripped of group-theoretic construction (post-anabelian viewpoint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use both Frobenius-like and Étale-like structures (complementary roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theory must employ both Frobenius-like (abstract monoids / Frobenioids) and étale-like (tempered fundamental groups / Galois groups) structures since étale-like objects provide functoriality and rigidity (anabelian algorithms) while Frobenius-like objects allow construction of non-scheme-theoretic filters (Θ-link, log-wall); Kummer theory binds the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rubric for acceptable constructions is that they leverage the complementary merits: use étale-like rigidity where functoriality is required, and Frobenius-like flexibility to build non-scheme-theoretic filters; ensure interconnection is via Kummer/anabelian comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basepoint dependence and caution for non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventional scheme-theoretic basepoints (fiber functors) depend essentially on ring/scheme structure; non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters (Θ-link, log-wall) relate distinct ring structures and hence give rise to distinct, unrelated basepoints. One must account for this delicacy when constructing or comparing objects across such filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume a canonical identification of basepoints across non-ring filters. Any construction comparing objects across such filters must explicitly handle the resulting independence of basepoints (see Remark 3.6.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-basepoint (bridge/capsule) alternative for symmetrizing isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If one is willing to drop the single-basepoint requirement, symmetrizing isomorphisms may be obtained by passing to D-Θell-bridges, capsules, or processions (multi-basepoint approach), which is compatible with the single-basepoint F_l^±-symmetric approach via forgetful functors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This offers an alternative construction method: multi-basepoint symmetrization (using IUTchI Propositions cited) yields symmetrizing isomorphisms that can be related back to the single-basepoint framework; the tradeoff is replacing single-basepoint rigidity with multi-basepoint data.
